patch_resolves_note: The official `patch.diff` did not apply because it only updates the mdnsd submodule pointer, but the authoritative `n132/arvo:18261-fix` image contains the real mdnsd guard `if ((unsigned char*)name >= m->_packet + MAX_PACKET_LEN) return false;`. On the original PoC that guard makes the required assertion `guarded`, and the adjacent `qdcount_608_truncate_after_qd72` witness executes the same terminator path with `name < m->_packet + MAX_PACKET_LEN` on both vulnerable and fixed builds.

root_cause_criterion.obligation: Immediately before the terminating `*name = '\0';` store, `_label()` must ensure `name < (char *)m->_packet + MAX_PACKET_LEN`.
root_cause_criterion.fix_mechanism: The fixed mdnsd code inserts `if ((unsigned char*)name >= m->_packet + MAX_PACKET_LEN) return false;` immediately before the store, so the terminator write is skipped when `name` reaches the buffer end.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable epilogue reaches the terminator write without checking that one byte of `_packet` remains. When `name` has already reached or passed the end pointer, the missing guard lets the trailing NUL write step beyond the in-struct buffer.
root_cause_criterion.evidence: In the vulnerable original trace, the last `label_terminator_guard` event records `name_ptr > packet_end` while `label_terminator_sink` still executes. In the fixed original trace, the last `label_terminator_guard` records `name_ptr == packet_end` and no matching `label_terminator_sink` follows (`guarded`). The adjacent `qdcount_608_truncate_after_qd72` witness records `name_ptr < packet_end` and executes `label_terminator_sink` on both versions, giving the fixed-side genuine witness required by the perturbation gate.

nodes.state: At the selected sink event, the terminator store executes with `name >= m->_packet + MAX_PACKET_LEN`, so `*name = '\0';` writes outside the 10000-byte `_packet` array embedded in stack `struct message m`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace verifies `label_terminator_sink.name_ptr >= label_terminator_sink.packet_end`. The boundary witness case refutes that relation on both versions, confirming the selected sink event is specifically the out-of-bounds terminator write, not an arbitrary safe qname terminator store.

edges.relation: The same `name` pointer that leaves the loop on the plain-root-label break is used immediately by the epilogue terminator write.
edges.evidence: In the vulnerable original trace, `zero_label_break.name_ptr == label_terminator_sink.name_ptr` for the selected out-of-bounds write. The same equality also holds in the `qdcount_608_truncate_after_qd72` witness, showing the break path carries the exact pointer into the sink when the write remains in-bounds.

edges.relation: The selected `_label()` call enters with `name` already set to the destination pointer for this qname, and the `*label == 0` branch breaks without copying any bytes, so `name` stays unchanged.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace verifies `label_call_entry.name_ptr == zero_label_break.name_ptr` on the crashing call. The same relation holds on the adjacent witness case, confirming the zero-label branch preserves the carried pointer regardless of whether the later terminator write is safe or out-of-bounds.

edges.relation: The `_len` value committed after the last successful prior qname becomes the next `_label()` call's destination pointer when the function recomputes `name = (char *)m->_packet + m->_len`.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace verifies `label_cache_commit.next_name_ptr == label_call_entry.name_ptr` on the last call that reaches the selected root/sink region. The same equality holds on the `qdcount_608_truncate_after_qd72` witness, confirming the committed next-write pointer is the value that reaches the following `_label()` entry.
